risk_if_not_implemented: Without Prevent Alterations, embedded and IoT technologies may operate with unknown, insecure or unmonitored configurations, creating exploitable footholds. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Unauthorized Modification / Loss of System Integrity (R-AM-2), System / Data Compromise (Technical Vector) (R-BC-4), System / Service Compromise (R-EX-7), OT Safety / Process Availability Failure (R-OT-1), Loss of Authenticity / Provenance (R-IP-5), and most likely increases susceptibility to Malicious Cyber Activity (MT-2), Technical / Mechanical Failure (MT-10), Operational Technology (OT) / Industrial Control System (ICS) Attack (MT-30).

compensating_control_1.name: Integrity Assurance & Enforcement (IAE)
compensating_control_1.description:
Automated mechanisms exist to:
(1) Identify unauthorized deviations from an approved secure baseline configuration; and
(2) Implement automated resiliency actions to remediate the unauthorized change.
compensating_control_1.justification: Integrity Assurance & Enforcement (IAE) (CFG-08.2) provides configuration hardening that compensates for the absence of Prevent Alterations (EMB-09) by eliminating unnecessary services and enforcing secure settings to reduce inherent exposure. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Continuous Monitoring
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of enterprise-wide monitoring controls.
compensating_control_2.justification: Continuous Monitoring (MON-02) provides detective monitoring capability that compensates for the absence of Prevent Alterations (EMB-09) by identifying unauthorized, anomalous, or non-compliant activity that the primary control would have prevented. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
